multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which prompt is most likely to produce a reproducible result?

choice.div: "Write a 150-word reply to this customer, keeping the dates below, ending with the next step and an owner."
"Write a good reply to this customer."

div.p: Audience, length, preserved facts, and a finish line are all stated. The others leave the definition of good to the model.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Why does one example of good output usually beat several adjectives?

choice.div: It shows length, structure and detail at once, where adjectives are ambiguous.
It lets the model copy the text without thinking.

div.p: An example is a concrete target. "Concise" is a judgment the model has to guess.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: What does a "definition of done" add to a brief?

choice.div: A testable finish line: what the reader must be able to do after reading.
A guarantee that the facts are correct.
A longer prompt, which always improves output.

div.p: The finish line makes the result checkable. It does not verify facts — that is still the reviewer's job.

choiceresponse.p: Which belong in a usable brief? Select all that apply.

choice.div: Constraints such as length and what must not change.
What the reader must be able to do afterwards.
A request to "be creative" with no other limit.

div.p: Context, constraints, an example and a finish line make a brief. Unbounded creativity removes the constraints that make output usable.
